mechanical_extraction_proof.claim: Refactor is MECHANICAL EXTRACTION with NO behavioral changes

evidence.proof: All 8 audio members (transport_, player_, previewMixer_, masterMixer_, resampler_, sequencerEngine_, bufferSource_, plus formatManager_, thumbCache_, reader_) have NO dependencies on other SampleBrowserPage members. They form a closed audio graph.
Only &player_ connects to AudioDeviceManager. Moving player_ to new class = move entire audio dependency. No other member talks to device manager.
SampleBrowserPage has PUBLIC methods (playFile, stopPlayback, triggerOneShot, etc.) that encapsulate audio. Moving audio to separate class = extract these methods and pass AudioEngine reference.
masterMixer_ + sequencerEngine_ setup in constructor (lines 1426-1428) happens BEFORE ensureAudioReady() (line 1430). Order is NOT dependent on UI members. Can move to AudioEngine constructor.
stopAndReleaseAudioSafely() is 10-step atomic sequence (lines 1574-1635). Each step is pure audio domain. Entire sequence can move to AudioEngine destructor with zero changes.

Audio members NEVER access: tiles_, selectedSet_, folderTreeView_, eqDivider_, variationMgr_, etc. (UI state). UI methods NEVER call audio setup directly (only via ensureAudioReady which already exists as indirection).

what_breaks_if_NOT_extracted: Audio logic mixed with UI logic = harder to test audio in isolation
Audio chain becomes harder to reuse (WavePreviewPage/EngineLabPage duplicate transport_/player_/resampler_ code)
Standalone app carries UI page lifecycle tied to audio lifetime (fragile)
what_stays_the_same: AudioDeviceManager still receives single player_ callback
Audio device sees ZERO change - same flow, same callback timing, same sample rates
File playback works identically - transport_.setSource() still reads disk with reader_
Sequencer timing unchanged - sequencerEngine_ still in masterMixer_
OneShot previews unchanged - temporary audio sources still work
Teardown sequence identical - same 10 steps, same timing, same atomicity

conclusion.reason: Audio chain is completely self-contained. All UI-audio communication goes through public methods. Moving audio to separate class is a straightforward ownership transfer with no behavioral changes.
conclusion.remaining_risk: 5% - Complex systems can surprise. Require full integration test of audio playback in standalone app (play file, stop, oneshot, sequencer) BEFORE shipping.
